recent_candidates.excerpt: Sponsored by The New York Historical [https://nyhistory.org/about/david-m-rubenstein-prize] In the Review’s August 20 issue, David Cole surveys the Supreme Court’s 2025–2026 term [https://www.nybooks.com/articles/2026/08/20/close-calls-us-supreme-court-david-cole/]. How’s the judicial branch dealing with the country’s slide into autocracy? The term just concluded offered good news and bad news. The good news is that the Court will sometimes check Trump when he acts unlawfully. In this sense, it functioned as a court, not as a politically partisan institution. That is essential to the preservation of the rule of law, and should not be discounted. Limits on presidential power are essential to a constitutional democracy, but so, too, are limits on the Court’s power.
